title: Multi‑Horizon Warmup and Capacity Orchestration Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This playbook describes a repeatable, operational pattern we call 'multi-horizon warmup' for Redwood's inference platform. It covers goals, telemetry and dashboard panels to create, automated and manual orchestration steps, SLOs and alerting thresholds, rollback criteria, and a short roadmap for improving warmup fidelity. Use this when launching new tenants, onboarding models or rolling out regionwide capacity changes.

Why multi-horizon warmup?

- Inference workloads have distinct 'horizons' where different preparatory actions reduce tail latency or token cost:
  - Seconds-to-minutes: connection pools, kernel JIT, process hot paths.
  - Minutes-to-hours: KV cache warm (prefixes), batching affinity, model shard residency.
  - Hours-to-days: thermal/availability stabilization, learned cache cohorts for tenants, offline optimizer replays.
- Treating warmup as a single step causes either over-provisioning (cost) or under-preparedness (latency/regressions). Multi-horizon warmup stages let us apply different controls and measurement hooks at each timescale.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to: hosted and dedicated pools, regional capacity expansions, tenant onboarding (>1000 monthly tokens), large model swaps, prefetch cohort rollouts.
- Not intended for: trivial config-only deploys (<5% expected traffic), or single-VM testbeds.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner_team: eng-platform (capacity and operator automation).
- Secondary owners: eng-serving-runtime (kernel/JIT), eng-sre (SLO monitoring), customer-success (tenant verification).
- On-call escalation chain: platform-oncall -> runtime-engineering -> eng-sre (see runbook links).

Goals and acceptance criteria

1) Within the short-horizon window (0–10 minutes after activation):
   - 95th token latency for cold-primed requests must be <= 1.5x steady-state 95p baseline.
   - Connection pool utilisation > 60% for tenant traffic.
2) Within the medium-horizon window (10 minutes–4 hours):
   - KV cache hit rate for pinned prefixes >= 85% (for workloads that expose prefixes).
   - Batch formation latency <= 50ms for batchable routes.
3) Within the long-horizon window (4 hours–72 hours):
   - Sustained throughput reaches expected capacity curve within 24 hours with no >5% tail-latency regressions.

Instrumentation and dashboard panels (minimum required)

Create a dashboard named: "Warmup: <cluster/tenant/model> — Multi‑Horizon View" with these panels:

- Live token latency heatmap (per-region, per-model).
- Connection pool state (idle/active/queued).
- KV cache hit-rate (prefix-level if available).
- Batch size distribution and batch latency percentiles.
- Warmup progress KPI: staged completion (short/medium/long).
- Cost delta estimator: predicted vs measured token cost during warmup.

Suggested alert rules (examples)

1) Short-horizon alert: "warmup-short-latency-regression"
   - Trigger when 95p token latency > 1.8x baseline for > 3 minutes AND connection pool utilisation < 40%.
   - Priority: P2; Notify: platform-oncall.
2) Medium-horizon alert: "warmup-cache-not-warming"
   - Trigger when KV cache hit rate < 50% after 30 minutes for known-prefix workloads.
   - Priority: P3; Notify: owner_team + customer-success if affected tenant.
3) Long-horizon alert: "warmup-sla-slope-miss"
   - Trigger when steady-state throughput plateau after 24 hours is < 90% of expected commit for > 2 hours.
   - Priority: P1; page eng-sre and runtime-engineering.

Operator workflows (playbook)

Pre-step: create the warmup ticket in the platform tracker with: target cluster, tenant(s), model(s), horizon timelines, expected traffic profile and rollback trigger thresholds. Attach a baseline snapshot.

Short-horizon (0–10 minutes) — automated first pass
1) Activate routing with gradual ramp flag (weight=0.1 -> 1.0 over 10 minutes) using the routing API:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/gradual -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLATFORM_TOKEN" -d '{"target": "cluster-nyc-1", "traffic_weight": 0.1, "ramp_minutes": 10, "validation": "latency"}'

2) Trigger kernel/JIT prime job if model variant supports it:
   - /srv/tools/runtime-prime --model model-id --p90-seqs 4
3) Verify connection pool and worker spin-up panels; if pools not healthy after 6 minutes, escalate to runtime-engineering.

Medium-horizon (10 minutes–4 hours) — prefetch and affinity
1) Start prefix prefetch jobs for top N prefixes derived from tenant's historical promptsets (N default 50). Example config: 

{
  "job": "prefix-prefetch",
  "tenant": "acme-corp",
  "target_prefixes": ["home_page_summary_v1", "search_prompt_v2"],
  "concurrency": 8,
  "rate_limit": "200r/s"
}

2) Monitor KV cache hit-rate; if below target, increase concurrency by +2 and re-evaluate after 20 minutes.
3) Enable batch affinity (sticky-binning heuristics) with conservative thresholds: prefer max_latency 30ms and min_batch_size 8.

Long-horizon (4 hours–72 hours) — cohort and thermal stabilization
1) Run cohort-learning job to create tenant warmset fingerprints for automated future onboarding. Persist as a "warmset-vX" artifact.
2) For dedicated pools, check GPU thermal telemetry and pre-warm NVMe-backed model shards to reduce I/O stalls.
3) Validate cost delta estimator; ensure unit cost for warmup period remains within 15% of normal unit economics unless approved.

Rollback and safety gates

- Immediate rollback triggers (perform automatic rollback and page on-call):
  - P95 tail latency > 3x baseline for > 5 minutes.
  - Error rate increase > 500 rps above baseline or > 2% absolute increase.
- Manual rollback triggers (operator decision):
  - KV cache not improving after two scaled prefetch attempts.
  - Cost delta estimator projecting > 30% incremental spend vs projected.

Operator checklists (condensed)

- Pre-rollout checklist:
  1) Attach baseline snapshot and expected traffic profile.
  2) Confirm prefetch job seed prefixes are sourced and validated.
  3) Schedule communications with affected on-call windows.
- During rollout checklist:
  1) Watch short-horizon panels; confirm kernel prime succeeded.
  2) Confirm batch formation and pool utilisation targets.
  3) Track cost delta and update ticket notes every hour.
- Post-rollout checklist:
  1) Confirm warmset artifact created and stored.
  2) Run a short regression: compare sample prompts vs pre-rollout answers for quality drift.
  3) Close warmup ticket and annotate lessons-learned.

Concrete runbook commands and snippets

- View warmup dashboard (Grafana):
  - Open: https://grafana.internal.redwood/warmup-dashboard?cluster=cluster-nyc-1&tenant=acme-corp
- Trigger a targeted rollback via CLI:
  - redwoodctl routing rollback --ticket 12345 --reason "latency spike"
- Sample prefetch orchestration (Kubernetes CronJob snippet):
  apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
  kind: CronJob
  metadata:
    name: prefix-prefetch-acme
  spec:
    schedule: "*/15 * * * *"
    jobTemplate:
      spec:
        template:
          spec:
            containers:
            - name: prefetch
              image: redwood/prefetch:stable
              args: ["--tenant", "acme-corp", "--concurrency", "8"]
            restartPolicy: OnFailure

Telemetry queries (examples)

- KV cache hit-rate (PromQL):
  sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{cluster="cluster-nyc-1", tenant="acme-corp"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{cluster="cluster-nyc-1", tenant="acme-corp"}[5m]))
- Batch latency p95 (PromQL):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",cluster="cluster-nyc-1"}[5m])) by (le))

Postmortem and retrospective guidance (how to capture learning)

- Template to capture: timeline of actions (with exact timestamps), top 3 metrics that failed/succeeded, operator decisions, and suggested configuration deltas.
- Run a 2-week rolling retrospective after first 50 warmups to tune heuristics and thresholds. Capture retrospective in the platform retrospective board and tag with label "warmup-learning".

Roadmap (next 12 months)

- Q2 2026: automated warmset synthesis — automatically derive top prefixes from anonymized prompt telemetry and auto-seed prefetch jobs.
- Q3 2026: warmup cost forecasting model — attach confidence bands and estimated spend.
- Q4 2026: warmup-as-a-service API — tenant self-service warmups with opt-in safety gates.

Appendices

A) Minimal SLO/threshold table

| Horizon | Key metric | Acceptance threshold | Escalation window | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Short | p95 token latency | <= 1.5x baseline | 10m | platform-oncall |
| Medium | KV cache hit-rate | >= 85% | 2h | runtime-engineering |
| Long | Throughput curve | >= 90% expected | 24h | eng-platform |

B) Example ticket template fields

- ticket_id, cluster, tenant, model, expected_traffic_profile (CSV), warmup_horizons (short/medium/long), rollback_triggers, dashboards_link, owners, communication_plan, estimated_cost_budget.

C) Links and references

- Runtime prime tool: /internal/tools/runtime-prime
- Prefetch service spec: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/prefetch-spec-2025
- Oncall matrix and runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/operator-oncall-quick-reference-shell-helpers-and-scripts-2026

If you are executing a warmup for an enterprise customer, attach the customer-approved spend budget and notify Customer Success before starting medium-horizon prefetches. For questions about adding a new telemetry panel to the warmup dashboard, reach out to the author or the eng-platform dashboard squad.
